title: Heat Pump Rebates in Los Angeles 2026: Up to $2,500 per Ton from LADWP | HomePowerRebate
desc: LADWP pays $1,000 to $1,250 per ton for a ducted heat pump and $1,500 to $2,500 per ton for a mini-split, by efficiency tier. Ratings, permit and how to apply.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Los Angeles
lead: LADWP pays by the ton, and the amount climbs with the efficiency rating: $1,000 to $1,250 per ton for a ducted system and $1,500 to $2,500 per ton for a mini-split. The highest figure on LADWP's page needs a very efficient mini-split, so check the tier before you choose a model.
cards_intro: These figures come from the Consumer Rebate Program page of the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP), which we read on October 2, 2026. The increased amounts apply to equipment bought and installed on or after November 1, 2025. You must be an LADWP residential customer with an active electric meter.

cards.title: Ducted, split or packaged
cards.note: $1,000 at 15.2 SEER2 and 7.7 HSPF2, rising to $1,250 at 19.6 SEER2 and 8.9 HSPF2.

cards.title: Ductless mini-split or multi-split
cards.note: $1,500 at 15.2 SEER2 and 7.8 HSPF2, rising to $2,500 at 20.5 SEER2 and 9.1 HSPF2.

cards.title: Minimum to qualify
cards.note: With an AHRI certificate that matches the system components.

cards.title: Not eligible
cards.note: Packaged terminal heat pumps, new construction and accessory dwelling units do not qualify.

after_cards:
What the tiers are worth

A 3-ton ducted system at the entry tier earns 3 x $1,000 = $3,000, and at the top ducted tier 3 x $1,250 = $3,750. A 3-ton mini-split at the entry tier earns 3 x $1,500 = $4,500, and at the top tier 3 x $2,500 = $7,500. LADWP says a home or multi-residential building can claim more than one unit if it applies for them at one time.
sections: Pick the model by its ratings, not its price

The rebate rewards efficiency in steps. A mini-split that reaches 16 SEER2 and 8.1 HSPF2 earns $1,650 per ton, and one at 20.5 SEER2 and 9.1 HSPF2 earns $2,500. Ask your installer for the SEER2 and HSPF2 of the exact indoor and outdoor combination, and ask them to show the AHRI certificate. A model that is one step lower could cost you hundreds of dollars per ton, and a more efficient model can cost more up front, so compare the two sides before you buy.

LADWP wants a paid itemized invoice with the make and model and the AHRI certificate reference, the AHRI certificate itself, and a final approved Building and Safety permit. In Los Angeles that is a permit from the Department of Building and Safety (LADBS). Applications go online through your LADWP account or by mail, and must be postmarked within 12 months of purchase. LADWP can inspect the installation before it sends the check, so keep the equipment accessible.

LADWP serves most of the City of Los Angeles and runs its own rebates, which is why it differs from Glendale, Burbank and Pasadena next door. Glendale pays $1,000 per ton up to $5,000 for a gas swap (Glendale), Burbank pays $1,000 per ton up to $2,500 (Burbank), and Pasadena pays $170 per ton (Pasadena). LADWP has the only tiered scale and the highest per-ton ceiling. Its program line is (866) 484-0433, weekdays 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Los Angeles's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 7.9°C (about 46°F), and the coldest recorded day in that stretch was -0.1°C. A standard heat pump handles that, so you do not need a cold-climate model. The tier scale means you may be tempted to buy a bigger or fancier unit for the rebate. Do not. Ask for a written load calculation and buy the size the house needs.

LADWP's page points to the South Coast AQMD GO ZERO program, which it describes as up to $3,000 for a qualified heat pump, and to the Switch Is On site. We did not read the GO ZERO terms, so check them before you count on that. The federal 25C and 25D tax credits ended for spending after December 31, 2025, even where LADWP's page still mentions a federal credit. Statewide help from TECH Clean California and the federal HEEHRA program is fully reserved and takes new requests on hold only.
installers_intro: These Los Angeles heat pump and HVAC companies have the best Google ratings, listed by rating and then review count. We are not paid to list anyone. Ask each for the model's SEER2 and HSPF2, the AHRI certificate and who pulls the LADBS permit.
claim_heading: How to claim the LADWP rebate
claim_steps: Check that LADWP is your electric utility, and that the home is not new construction or an ADU.
Choose a heat pump that meets 15.2 SEER2 and 7.7 HSPF2, and ask for the AHRI certificate.
Have the system installed under a Building and Safety permit and get the permit finaled.
Collect the paid itemized invoice, the AHRI certificate and the final permit.
Apply through your LADWP online account, or mail the application, within 12 months of the purchase date.
Expect LADWP to inspect before it sends the rebate check.
faq: How much is the LADWP heat pump rebate?
$1,000 to $1,250 per ton for ducted systems and $1,500 to $2,500 per ton for mini-splits, depending on the SEER2 and HSPF2 tier.
15.2 SEER2 and 7.7 HSPF2, with a matching AHRI certificate.
Yes. LADWP asks for a final approved Building and Safety permit.
Does it apply to a new home or an ADU?
No. New construction and accessory dwelling units are excluded.
Can I claim more than one unit?
LADWP says a home or multi-residential building may claim more than one unit if it applies for them at one time.
